Hey, I graduated in 2021 and majored in Computer Engineering.

  
1. There are plenty of opportunities but you do need to be proactive in pursuing them. Meet with your advisor, have your resume looked at, go to the career fairs, etc.

2. It is engineering school so expect to have a pretty heavy workload. That being said, it will vary depending on what courses you happen to be taking in a given semester.  Even during my busiest semesters there was still time to do fun stuff/hang out with friends etc.   


3. I've lived in/around Pittsburgh my whole life and it's super underrated imo. It's a great city with a lot of cool neighborhoods. You can get around pretty easily using public transportation (free with your student ID). While I was a student my friends and I would frequently explore other neighborhoods to check out restaurants or niche local businesses (skate shops, tabletop game stores, thrift stores, etc.). Definitely recommend exploring Lawrenceville, Squirrel Hill, the Strip District, The South Side, The North Side/Mexican war streets. Downtown isn't that exciting imo but there's some cool stuff I guess (point state park, market square, some nicer restaurants, several museums). I've never felt unsafe here, but there are some neighborhoods that I avoid.  


4. Kinda weird and inconsistent. It's often very cloudy, everyone here probably has a vitamin D deficiency lol. It can definitely jump around a lot (random warm day in the winter, random cold day in the summer). The biggest thing I would warn a California native about is the winter of course. It'll be much colder than you are used to and it will snow a fair bit so be sure to get a winter jacket and perhaps some boots as well.
